### 1. Scene
Sliced cooked chicken with rocket/arugula salad, broccoli, a few chickpeas and red pepper pieces, with a glossy, possibly mustard-based dressing.

### 2. Vessel
A large rounded-square dinner plate, approximately **26–28 cm across**. Using a 26 cm circular approximation gives an area of **3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm²**.

### 3–7. Items, area, volume, weight and energy
The area allocations below total **60% of the plate**, consistent with the substantial bare rim. Dressing area is allocated separately from the chicken and greens to avoid double-counting.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked chicken slices | 16% | 85 cm² × 1.6 cm = 136 ml | 1.0 | 136 g | 170 | 231 kcal |
| Rocket/arugula | 29% | 154 cm² × 2 cm = 308 ml | 0.15 | 46 g | 25 | 12 kcal |
| Broccoli | 9% | 48 cm² × 2.4 cm = 115 ml | 0.6 | 69 g | 35 | 24 kcal |
| Chickpeas | 1% | 5 cm² × 1.4 cm = 7 ml | 0.7 | 5 g | 164 | 8 kcal |
| Red pepper pieces | 2% | 11 cm² × 0.9 cm = 10 ml | 0.6 | 6 g | 30 | 2 kcal |
| Oily, mustard-like dressing | 3% | 16 cm² × 0.95 cm = 15 ml | 1.0 | 15 g | 350 | 53 kcal |

### 8. Sanity check
**Approximately 277 g and 330 kcal** is plausible for the visible chicken portion, small broccoli serving and loose salad. Dressing composition is the largest energy uncertainty; a reasonable overall range is **270–410 kcal**.
